sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0.1, PCI Security Standards Council document library
sources.note: v4.0.1 is the currently published version: the PCI SSC request for comments of 3 June to 20 July 2026 is on "the currently-published version", v4.0.1. The standard itself is behind the library's licence page and was not fetched; requirement numbers and the 6.4.1 to 6.4.2 change come from the RFC notice and secondary sources.

sources.title: RFC instructions for the currently published PCI DSS v4.0.1
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (with Amd 1:2024), Annex A; control names as in ISO/IEC 27002:2022
sources.note: Titles checked against public control indexes; iso.org refused automated access. Amd 1:2024 (climate action) changes clauses 4.1 and 4.2, not Annex A.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), EUR-Lex
sources.note: Article titles and the test types in Article 25(1) read from the EUR-Lex text.

sources.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190, RTS on threat-led penetration testing
sources.note: Read to confirm that AttackLedger tests are not TLPT; nothing maps to Article 26 or 27.

strengths.full: The result alone answers the control's test; nothing else is needed.
strengths.partial: The result answers a defined part of the control's test; the rest needs other evidence.
strengths.supporting: The result is relevant and can corroborate other evidence; it does not answer the test.

controls.text: Article 24, General requirements for digital operational resilience testing
controls.note: The testing programme, its independence, remediation and yearly coverage need other evidence.

controls.text: Article 25, Testing of ICT tools and systems
controls.note: Vulnerability assessments and penetration testing are among the tests Article 25(1) lists. AttackLedger tests are not threat-led penetration testing (Article 26, RTS 2025/1190).
The entity identifies and inventories its own assets; external discovery can only be compared with that.
Relevant to access limitation and strong authentication, Article 9(4)(c) and (d).

controls.text: Inventory of information and other associated assets
controls.note: Hosts and applications found in testing can be compared with the inventory; they are not the inventory.

controls.text: Security testing in development and acceptance
controls.note: Only when the test is part of the development or release acceptance process.
Testing identifies vulnerabilities; evaluating them and acting in time need other evidence.

controls.text: A penetration testing methodology is defined, documented and implemented
controls.note: The method followed is the evidence for application-layer testing; network-layer and segmentation testing are not covered.

Application-layer part only, and only when testing is from outside the network. Frequency, tester qualification and independence, and network-layer testing need other evidence. A bug bounty can add to this test but does not replace it.

controls.text: Strong cryptography protects PAN in transit over open, public networks
controls.note: Only for hosts that receive or send PAN. A TLS test shows the protocol and certificate state at test time.

controls.text: Software engineering techniques prevent or mitigate common software attacks
controls.note: Assessed mainly from procedures and developers; a test shows whether those attack types were found.
